**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The document does contain a usable Vendor indemnity (Section 10, ¶p0046–p0052) with procedures (Section 11, ¶p0053–p0055):

- **Vendor indemnity present and broad** — Kubient defends/indemnifies/holds harmless Customer and its officers, directors, agents and employees against third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and acts/omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors.
- **IP infringement covered** — via the Services/Platform limbs plus the breach-of-warranty limb, which picks up the Section 9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty covering the Service and deliverables; 9(b)(iii) (data security) and 9(b)(ix) (compliance with Law) similarly feed the indemnity, matching the preferred position's (a)–(d).
- **Standard procedure** — prompt notice (expressly not a condition to recovery), indemnitor control of defence, no settlement admitting our liability without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost.
- **No sub-cap** — Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion, so the fallback 3× super-cap is not needed.
- **Customer indemnity acceptable** — keyed to our Content/Properties, our misuse and our own breach.

Minor points noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the Creative limb of the Vendor indemnity is softened by "to the best of its knowledge," and limb (v) of the Customer indemnity ("acts or omissions of Customer") is somewhat wider than the playbook's ideal narrow scope. Neither is material enough to redline given the clause otherwise sits at the preferred position.
